source.title: String length() counts emoji as two characters instead of one

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
### Description

The `length()` string extension is documented as "Returns the character count of a string", but it is implemented as `return value.length;`, which counts UTF-16 code units instead of characters. Any character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane (an emoji, or an astral CJK ideograph) is stored as a surrogate pair, so `length()` reports `2` for a single character.

This shows up in ordinary workflows: text coming from APIs, chat messages, form fields or CSV files often contains emoji. A user who writes `{{ $json.message.length() }}` in a Set or IF node to validate, truncate or display text length gets the wrong number, and comparisons such as "the message must be at most one character" are wrong.

### To Reproduce

In any expression field, evaluate (each string below contains one emoji, U+1F600):

```
{{ "😀".length() }}
{{ "a😀b".length() }}
```

Actual results: `2` and `4`. The same happens for any astral-plane character, for example CJK Extension B ideographs such as U+20000.

### Expected behavior

`length()` should return the number of characters (Unicode code points), as its documentation states:

- `{{ "😀".length() }}` -> `1`
- `{{ "a😀b".length() }}` -> `3`
- `{{ "String".length() }}` -> `6` (ASCII unchanged)
- a two-character BMP string (e.g. two CJK characters) -> `2` (BMP non-ASCII unchanged)

Strings containing only BMP characters must keep their current results; only astral-plane characters (surrogate pairs) should be counted as one character.

### Notes

The string extensions are intentionally mirrored between `packages/workflow/src/extensions/string-extensions.ts` and `packages/@n8n/expression-runtime/src/extensions/string-extensions.ts`; both implementations are affected.

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: One behavior detail worth deciding before changing this: should “character count” mean Unicode code points or user-perceived grapheme clusters? Code-point counting would make `"😀"` return 1, but a flag emoji or a letter plus a combining mark can still count as 2. The issue examples establish the surrogate-pair case, but not those multi-code-point characters. Also, the current implementation is `value.length` in the workflow extension; the file says it is intentionally mirrored in the expression-runtime package, so both paths need to agree.

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: The current `length()` implementation uses `value.length` in both mirrored extension files, so it counts UTF-16 code units. The expected `1` for `"😀"` points to counting Unicode code points (`Array.from(value).length` would do that); grapheme-cluster counting would be a different contract, since flags and combining sequences can contain multiple code points. Which meaning should this expression use? Whichever is chosen, the workflow and expression-runtime implementations need to stay in sync.
